 - **Alive Players:** 8.

 - **Day Discussion:** Roundrobin. Players speak in round-robin order for 2 round(s). The starting speaker rotates to the next player in the list for each subsequent day, but remains the same for all rounds within that day.

 - **Night Werewolf Vote:** Sequential Voting. Players vote one by one. Player with the most votes after all have voted is eliminated. The starting voter rotates to the next player in the list for each subsequent voting phase. Ties result in no elimination.
 - The following explain the function of each role.
  * Role name Seer - team Villagers - Each night, may inspect one player to learn their true role.
  * Role name Werewolf - team Werewolves - Each night, collaborates with fellow werewolves to vote on eliminating one player.
  * Role name Villager - team Villagers - No special abilities. Participates in the daily vote to eliminate a suspected werewolf.
  * Role name Doctor - team Villagers - Each night, may protect one player from a werewolf attack. Doctor is NOT allowed to save themselves during night time. Doctor is NOT allowed to save the same player on consecutive nights.
 - If a player is exiled in the day, their role will be revealed.
 - If a player is eliminated at night, their role will be revealed.

First, let's be honest about what happened: Casey was the FIRST person to name Jamie. I agreed with Casey's logic. Then Alex agreed. Then Charlie agreed. Then Jordan, Taylor, and Kai ALL voted Jamie too. Every single player except Jamie voted Jamie. So why am I being singled out when Casey started the push and everyone followed?

Second - and this is critical - Jordan was our Seer, and the wolves eliminated them last night. That is the most important information on this board right now, and I notice Taylor and Kai are both trying to keep the conversation focused on me instead of on that. The wolves specifically targeted the Seer. Ask yourselves: who benefits from us spending today relitigating yesterday's mis-exile instead of analyzing who eliminated Jordan?

Third, think about wolf strategy. If Alex and I were both wolves, why would we BOTH loudly push a Villager on Day 1? That's guaranteed to make us both look terrible after the flip. I understand the suspicion, and I said yesterday I'd accept scrutiny if Jamie flipped Villager. So let me address this head-on.

First, let's be honest about what happened: Casey was the FIRST person to name Jamie. I agreed with Casey's logic. Then Alex agreed. Then Charlie agreed. Then Jordan, Taylor, and Kai ALL voted Jamie too. Every single player except Jamie voted Jamie. So why am I being singled out when Casey started the push and everyone followed?

Second - and this is critical - Jordan was our Seer, and the wolves eliminated them last night. That is the most important information on this board right now, and I notice Taylor and Kai are both trying to keep the conversation focused on me instead of on that. The wolves specifically targeted the Seer. Ask yourselves: who benefits from us spending today relitigating yesterday's mis-exile instead of analyzing who eliminated Jordan?

Third, think about wolf strategy. If Alex and I were both wolves, why would we BOTH loudly push a Villager on Day 1? That's guaranteed to make us both look terrible after the flip. Smart wolf pairs split - one pushes, one distances. The fact that we're both under fire now would be the worst possible wolf play.

My actual reads: I'm most suspicious of Taylor and Kai right now. They've been steering the narrative toward me since the moment Day 2 started, almost like they had this planned. One of them could easily be a wolf using the Jamie misexile as cover to eliminate another Villager today. Casey I give some credit for owning the mistake, but Casey also started the Jamie wagon - so if pushing Jamie is wolfy, that applies to Casey too.

We cannot afford another misexile. Kai said it - if we get this wrong, wolves win. So let's actually discuss the Seer eliminate and stop tunnel-visioning on me just because I agreed with a read that turned out wrong.

That is the most important information on this board right now, and I notice Taylor and Kai are both trying to keep the conversation focused on me instead of on that. Smart wolf pairs split - one pushes, one distances. The fact that we're both under fire now would be the worst possible wolf play.

One of them could easily be a wolf using the Jamie misexile as cover to eliminate another Villager today. We cannot afford another misexile. Kai said it - if we get this wrong, wolves win. So let's actually discuss the Seer eliminate and stop tunnel-visioning on me just because I agreed with a read that turned out wrong.

Casey started the Jamie push and has owned the mistake - that reads more village to me. Taylor and Kai flagged the risk before the flip, which is a strong village signal.

I'm currently leaning Quinn, but I want to hear from Charlie before I commit. Charlie, who's your wolf pair read right now?

Kai says I'm deflecting by bringing up Jordan's elimination. But Jordan was our Seer - that's the single most important piece of information we have. Dismissing it as 'zero info' is wrong. The wolves identified and eliminated our Seer on Night 1. That matters for figuring out who the wolves are.

Alex's move today concerns me the most. Yesterday Alex and I were aligned. Here's what I'll say: if I flip Villager - and I will - please look hard at whoever pushed hardest to eliminate me today without engaging with the actual logic. Look at Charlie, who has played the safest game possible while always landing on the majority. Look at Kai, who has been the most aggressive voice against me. And look at Alex's convenient pivot.

I've said my piece. I can't force you to believe me, but another Villager exile today ends this game for the village.
